newsitem.title: USA: Nationwide Insurance offers fair housing settlement.
newsitem.headline: Nationwide Insurance offers fair housing settlement.

text.p: The Justice Department said Monday that Nationwide Mutual Insurance Co. is offering to settle a suit involving discrimination against minorities by investing $13 million in 10 inner city neighborhoods.
It also promises to change the ways it markets homeowner insurance and to ensure that minority neighborhoods get equal access to insurance, Attorney General Janet Reno announced.

In a complaint filed in U.S. District Court in Columbus, Ohio, the Justice Department charged that Nationwide, the fifth biggest home insurance company, restricted the neighborhoods where policies could be written and instructed agents to avoid doing business in minority neighborhoods.
State Farm, Allstate and American Family Insurance Co. have all reached similar agreements with the government after accusations that they discriminated.
Nationwide agreed to invest $13.2 million in communities with the money to be administered by community groups when the court agrees to the settlement.
The funds will be used to help minority home buyers with down payments, closing costs, cheaper loans and other help.
